======================================================================
0. PROVENANCE AND CONTROL
======================================================================

This document develops the user-selected witness type A.

It is a new derivative formalization. It is not recovery of the missing
original EMB_CC-03 source and is not canonically accepted.

The construction is constrained by the surviving Volume II definitions:

- configurations are admissible relational structures;
- configuration embeddings are injective and preserve and reflect the
  selected apartness relation;
- CC(C1,C2)=1 iff an admissible amalgamation exists;
- D_CC is the compatibility diagram;
- R := colim(D_CC) only when the required categorical construction exists.

No definition in the Frozen Core is modified.

======================================================================
1. AMBIENT CATEGORY AND EMBEDDINGS
======================================================================

Let C_METACORE be a selected category of admissible configurations.

An object C in C_METACORE is a configuration:
C = (S_C,#_C)

where S_C is its carrier and #_C is its selected apartness relation.

For configurations C1=(S1,#1) and C2=(S2,#2), an embedding
f:C1 -> C2 is an injective map f:S1 -> S2 satisfying:

x #1 y iff f(x) #2 f(y)

for all x,y in S1.

The biconditional is required. Preservation without reflection is not
sufficient for an embedding under the Volume II convention.

All morphisms used as legs of the candidate amalgamation witness are
embeddings. No assumption is made that every abstract category morphism
in every possible realization is an embedding.

======================================================================
2. FINITE DIAGRAM
======================================================================

Let J be a finite category and let:

Delta:J -> C_METACORE

be a functor.

Finite means that Ob(J) and Mor(J) are finite.

For every object j in J, Delta(j) is a configuration.
For every arrow u:j->k, Delta(u) is an embedding.

The diagram may encode:
- a pair of configurations with no specified common subconfiguration;
- a span over a specified common subconfiguration;
- a larger finite compatibility pattern.

The shape of J must be explicitly stated for each application.
No canonical indexing category for D_CC is supplied by this checkpoint.

======================================================================
3. CANDIDATE WITNESS: ADMISSIBLE AMALGAMATING COCONE
======================================================================

DEFINITION A1 — AMALGAMATING COCONE

An admissible amalgamating cocone over Delta is a tuple:

W = (A, (eta_j)_{j in Ob(J)})

such that:

(A1) A is an object of C_METACORE.

(A2) For every j in Ob(J), eta_j:Delta(j)->A is an embedding.

(A3) For every arrow u:j->k in J, the cocone equation holds:

eta_k o Delta(u) = eta_j.

The apex A is the amalgamating configuration.
The maps eta_j are its structural embeddings.

The witness is the full tuple W, not merely the apex A. Different leg
families into the same apex may define different cocones.

DEFINITION A2 — DIAGRAM-RELATIVE AMALGAMATION SUFFICIENCY

Suff_A(Delta,W) iff W is an admissible amalgamating cocone over Delta
satisfying A1-A3.

Existence predicate:

Amalg(Delta) iff there exists W such that Suff_A(Delta,W).

This is a candidate realization of diagram-relative sufficiency. It is
not asserted to be the recovered original EMB_CC-03 predicate.

DEFINITION A3 — PAIRWISE COMPATIBILITY

For a selected compatibility diagram Delta_12 representing C1 and C2:

CC_A(C1,C2)=1 iff Amalg(Delta_12).

Otherwise:

CC_A(C1,C2)=0.

If a common subconfiguration C0 and embeddings
i1:C0->C1, i2:C0->C2 are specified, Delta_12 is the span:

C1 <-i1- C0 -i2-> C2.

An amalgam is then a configuration A and embeddings
m1:C1->A, m2:C2->A satisfying:

m1 o i1 = m2 o i2.

If no common subconfiguration is specified, the chosen diagram shape must
say so explicitly. A span must not be silently assumed.

======================================================================
4. STRONG AMALGAMATION IS NOT REQUIRED
======================================================================

The candidate definition requires embeddings and the cocone equations.
It does not require the images of different configurations to intersect
only in the image of their declared common part.

For a span, strong amalgamation would add:

m1(C1) intersect m2(C2) = m1(i1(C0)).

This is an additional condition and is NOT part of Suff_A.

Therefore:
ordinary admissible amalgamation != strong amalgamation.

The distinction preserves the existing status:
STRONG AMALGAMATION: NOT REQUIRED.

======================================================================
5. COMPARISON OF WITNESSES, MINIMALITY, AND LEASTNESS
======================================================================

Let:

W=(A,(eta_j))
V=(B,(theta_j))

be two admissible cocones over the same Delta.

DEFINITION A4 — WITNESS FACTORIZATION

Write W <=_Delta V iff there exists an embedding h:A->B such that:

h o eta_j = theta_j

for every j in Ob(J).

This relation is reflexive and transitive. It is generally a preorder,
not necessarily a partial order on raw cocone tuples.

Define equivalence of witnesses by:

W ~=_Delta V iff W <=_Delta V and V <=_Delta W.

For an embedding-based category, this identifies witnesses that are
isomorphic over the diagram, subject to the selected category's
monomorphism and isomorphism properties.

DEFINITION A5 — MINIMAL AMALGAMATION WITNESS

A witness W is minimal if there is no witness V such that:

V <=_Delta W

and not(V ~=_Delta W).

Minimality is therefore relative to factorization by embeddings over Delta.
It is not minimization of the cardinality of A unless a separate theorem
establishes that relationship.

DEFINITION A6 — LEAST AMALGAMATION WITNESS

A witness W_* is least if:

W_* <=_Delta V

for every admissible witness V over Delta.

Leastness is stronger than minimality.
It is an initial-object condition in the category/preorder of admissible
amalgamation witnesses and their over-Delta embedding factorizations.

No existence or uniqueness of a least witness is asserted here.

======================================================================
6. FINITENESS: EXACT STATEMENT
======================================================================

DEFINITION A7 — FINITE WITNESS

W=(A,(eta_j)) is finite iff the apex A has finite carrier and the
selected relational data on A is finite.

For a finite relational signature, finite carrier implies finite
relational data.

The finite diagram condition:

|Ob(J)| < infinity and |Mor(J)| < infinity

does NOT by itself imply that an admissible cocone exists.

It also does NOT imply that every admissible cocone has a finite apex.

The finite-witness assertion is:

FW(Delta) iff there exists a finite W with Suff_A(Delta,W).

This is an existence claim and must be proved for the selected category
and diagram. It is not included in the definition of sufficiency.

Important separation:

finite indexing diagram
!= finite apex
!= existence of an admissible amalgam
!= existence of a least amalgam.

If C_METACORE is deliberately restricted to finite configurations, every
existing witness in that selected category has a finite apex. This is a
property of that restricted realization, not a theorem that a witness
exists. The restriction must be declared before it is used.

======================================================================
7. FINITE APARTNESS REALIZATION: CONSTRUCTIVE POSITIVE TEST
======================================================================

Define FinApart as follows.

Objects:
finite sets S with |S|>=2, equipped with:

x # y iff x != y.

Morphisms:
injective maps.

These maps preserve and reflect #, so they are embeddings under the
Volume II convention.

Consider a span of finite configurations:

C1 <- C0 -> C2

with both span maps embeddings.

Construct the set-theoretic free amalgam:

A = (S1 disjoint-union S2) / ~

where the equivalence relation identifies the two copies of every
element in the image of C0 and makes no other identifications.

Equip A with:

x #_A y iff x != y.

The canonical maps:

m1:C1->A
m2:C2->A

are injective and preserve and reflect apartness.

They agree on C0:

m1 o i1 = m2 o i2.

A is finite because S1 and S2 are finite.

Therefore every finite span in this particular FinApart realization has
a finite admissible amalgam.

RESULT:
FINITE AMALGAM EXISTENCE: PROVED FOR THIS REALIZATION AND THIS SPAN CLASS.

SCOPE:
This result depends on the unrestricted class of finite sets with
apartness defined by inequality. It does not establish amalgamation for
every admissible subclass of C_METACORE, every apartness realization,
or the canonical OMEGA-ISOP category.

======================================================================
8. IMPORTANT DISTINCTION: AMALGAM IS NOT AUTOMATICALLY A COLIMIT
======================================================================

The free amalgam above is an admissible amalgam, but it is not generally
a categorical pushout in the category whose morphisms are embeddings.

Counterexample:

C0={0,1}
C1={0,1,p}
C2={0,1,q}

All structures use apartness x#y iff x!=y.

The free amalgam A identifies the two copies of 0 and 1, but keeps
p_A and q_A distinct.

Now let B={0,1,r}. Define embeddings:

f1:C1->B by p->r.
f2:C2->B by q->r.

They agree on C0.

A map h:A->B agreeing with both f1 and f2 would have to satisfy:

h(p_A)=r
h(q_A)=r.

Since p_A != q_A, h is not injective and therefore is not an embedding.

Thus the free amalgam does not have the categorical pushout universal
property inside the embedding-only category.

CONCLUSION:

admissible amalgam existence
does not imply
categorical pushout existence.

Accordingly, the core construction:

R := colim(D_CC)

still requires a separate indexing category, functor, morphism class,
and universal-property proof. The existence of pairwise amalgams alone
does not construct the required colimit.

This distinction is essential for preventing an invalid inference from
CC(C1,C2) to existence of R.

======================================================================
9. D_INFINITY RE-TEST UNDER THE COCONE PREDICATE
======================================================================

The previous baseline obstruction used the one-object category with:

End(X)=D_infinity=<a,b | a^2=e, b^2=e>.

A finite diagram Delta mapped two unrelated arrows to a and b.
The subcategory generated by {a,b} was infinite because ab has infinite
order.

That result concerns the closure of diagram image data under
subcategory composition.

It does not automatically refute the present cocone-witness predicate.

Use the same finite indexing category J with objects A,B,C,D and
nonidentity arrows:

u:A->B
v:C->D.

Let Delta map every object to X and:

Delta(u)=a
Delta(v)=b.

Choose apex X and cocone legs:

eta_B=e
eta_A=a
eta_D=e
eta_C=b.

Then:

eta_B o Delta(u) = e o a = a = eta_A
eta_D o Delta(v) = e o b = b = eta_C.

All legs are isomorphisms, hence monomorphisms, in the one-object group
category.

Therefore this finite diagram has a finite cocone witness in this
abstract category, although the subcategory generated by a and b is
infinite.

RESULT:
The D_infinity model refutes the unrestricted finite-generated-
subcategory-witness claim.

It does NOT refute finite cocone-witness existence in general.

It is not a CC-specific counterexample unless the selected CC
realization independently identifies its witnesses with the
subcategory-closure construction.

This re-test demonstrates that choosing the witness type changes the
mathematical problem. The old obstruction must not be carried over
without checking the new predicate.

======================================================================
10. JOINT WITNESS: INDIVIDUAL EXISTENCE IS NOT ENOUGH
======================================================================

A finite family Delta_1,...,Delta_n has a joint witness only if the
combined compatibility diagram admits one common cocone.

Individual witnesses:

Amalg(Delta_i) for every i

do not logically entail:

Amalg(Delta_1 union ... union Delta_n).

Simple categorical countermodel:

Let C be a discrete category with two distinct objects P and Q and
only identity morphisms.

Let Delta_P and Delta_Q be the one-object identity diagrams.

Each has an individual finite witness:
P witnesses Delta_P.
Q witnesses Delta_Q.

There is no common cocone for their disjoint union, because a cocone
would require an object receiving morphisms from both P and Q, and no
such object exists in C.

Therefore:

individual finite amalgams
does not entail
a joint amalgam.

A separate joint compatibility condition remains necessary.

This is a general categorical countermodel, not a claim about the
canonical OMEGA-ISOP realization.

======================================================================
11. WHAT THIS CANDIDATE NOW ESTABLISHES
======================================================================

DEFINED IN THIS CANDIDATE:
- finite diagram Delta:J->C_METACORE;
- admissible amalgamating cocone;
- diagram-relative amalgamation sufficiency Suff_A;
- pairwise CC_A relative to an explicit compatibility diagram;
- witness factorization;
- minimal witness;
- least witness;
- finite witness.

PROVED:
- the candidate cocone definition is well-typed;
- it generalizes a pairwise amalgam over a specified span;
- strong amalgamation is not required;
- finite spans have finite amalgams in the specific FinApart realization;
- admissible amalgam is not automatically categorical pushout;
- finite diagram does not automatically imply a common witness;
- D_infinity subcategory-closure obstruction does not automatically
  apply to cocone witnesses.

NOT PROVED:
- the candidate predicate is identical to the missing original
  EMB_CC-03 predicate;
- all objects in the canonical C_METACORE have finite carriers;
- finite amalgams exist in every canonical CC realization;
- minimal amalgams exist in every realization;
- least amalgams exist;
- the relevant colimit for D_CC exists;
- the canonical R construction follows from pairwise CC alone.

======================================================================
12. LOOP / ANTI-CIRCULARITY AUDIT
======================================================================

TARGET:
A finite diagram has a finite admissible amalgamation witness.

INVALID SHORTCUT:
J finite => finite apex.

VALID ROUTE:
1. Specify C_METACORE and its object class.
2. Specify the exact diagram Delta and its embeddings.
3. Construct an apex A in C_METACORE.
4. Construct all cocone legs eta_j.
5. Verify the cocone equations.
6. Verify that every leg is an embedding.
7. Verify that A is finite independently.

The FinApart proof satisfies these steps for its stated class.

TARGET:
A minimal amalgam is finite.

No general theorem is established.
Minimality is defined by factorization, not by cardinality.
A separate finite-support or rank argument, or a direct finite-amalgam
existence theorem together with an appropriate minimality argument, is
required.

TARGET:
A finite family has a finite common amalgam.

No inference from individual witnesses is permitted.
Joint cocone existence and finite apex must be checked directly or
proved from independent hypotheses.

D_INFINITY:
No longer used as a direct counterexample to the cocone predicate.
It remains a counterexample to the baseline subcategory-closure
predicate.

No desired conclusion has been inserted into a definition.

======================================================================
14. NEXT JUSTIFIED TESTS
======================================================================

TEST A — CATEGORY MATCH:
Determine whether the intended C_METACORE objects and morphisms are
exactly admissible configurations and the Volume II embeddings.

TEST B — PAIR DIAGRAM:
Recover or specify whether each CC pair is represented by a discrete
two-object diagram or by a span over a common subconfiguration.

TEST C — ADMISSIBLE APEX:
Specify all conditions an amalgamating apex must satisfy beyond being
an object of C_METACORE.

TEST D — FINITE EXISTENCE:
Test finite amalgamation in at least one nontrivial constrained
configuration class, not only FinApart.

TEST E — MINIMALITY:
Construct two incomparable minimal cocone witnesses or prove a
uniqueness/leastness result under explicit assumptions.

TEST F — JOINT COMPATIBILITY:
Test finite families using one combined diagram. Do not infer joint
existence from individual CC values.

TEST G — COLIMIT BOUNDARY:
Specify J, the functor D:J->C_METACORE, and the exact universal
property required for R := colim(D_CC). Do not substitute pairwise
amalgams for the colimit.

TEST H — SOURCE MATCH:
Compare every candidate definition against the original EMB_CC-03
source if it is recovered. Until then retain derivative status.
